title: Customer Hold Allowances by Build Class (Factory Production Orders)
content:
Factory Production Orders may be paused by the homeowner before production starts. How many holds an order may receive and how long one hold may run depend on the build class.

| Build class | Holds one order may receive | Longest single hold (calendar days from the hold start date) |
|---|---|---|
| Custom Size Build | 2 | 60 |
| Custom Color Build | 2 | 60 |
| Specialty Glass Build | 1 | 45 |
| Specialty Shape Build | 1 | 45 |
| Impact-Rated Build | 1 | 30 |
| Architectural Wood Build | 1 | 30 |

## Settings common to every class

- **Automatic release** — yes: a hold that reaches its maximum length is released automatically into the production queue.
- **Hold requote basis** — release date plus standard lead: the ship date set when a hold ends adds the class standard lead time, in business days, to the release date. This basis names the standard requote only; it does not by itself settle the ship date set when a hold is released.

## Points of reading

- The hold count is per order. A customer with two Custom Size Build orders may place up to 2 holds on each.
- In the Specialty Glass, Specialty Shape, Impact-Rated and Architectural Wood Build classes a single hold is the whole allowance.
- Hypothetical example: a Custom Color Build order whose hold started on the 1st day of a 31-day month reaches its 60-calendar-day maximum 60 days later; a hold on an Impact-Rated Build order started the same day reaches its maximum after 30 days.
